title: Information first, decoration never.
text: An element earns pixels by telling the reader something. Initial avatars, doc thumbnails, row glyphs, FAB, Share: cut. A real author photo is information; an initial is not.

title: Complete identifiers, never truncated.
text: PR titles wrap, never ellipsise. Repo + number always scannable. Branch means both ends: head → base. Diffstat always coloured.

title: Dense but calm meta.
text: All the facts (number, author, diffstat, checks, age) but never one cluttered line. Group, align, give variable fields fixed width.

title: Lists are the backbone.
text: Rows grouped by repo, chips for scope. Tappable rows look tappable (chevron, pressed state). Swipe actions are the fast path. No explanatory copy or empty-state prose under a populated list.

title: Sheets over the page, not new pages.
text: Bottom sheets for grouped actions, chat, composer, files. Dim everything beneath, uniformly, including the header and the trigger.

title: Words mean what they do.
text: Sections, not stops. Buttons name their effect. Cites say where they lead and are tappable. Every paragraph is labelled (Summary / Description).

title: Irreversible actions are never primary.
text: Merge lives behind the ⋯ menu. The bottom primary is the reviewing action (Review 4 files, Next).

title: No cards for numbers.
text: Stat tiles / KPI cards are ugly. No boxed mini-widgets; typographic hierarchy on a flat page.

title: The diff is the product.
text: Full-width lines, hunk expanders, word highlights, line numbers. Add/remove backgrounds clearly visible. Inline thread cards on their line. Files via a drawer or menu plus ‹ ›, never snapped tabs or horizontal swipe.

title: Composer: two modes.
text: Comment and Ask Pulls only. Split visual layout, not three text chips. No counters, no voice.

title: Not wanted, ever.
text: Voice/dictation. Suggestion mode. Share on PR/tour. “Up next” inside a tour. FAB with unclear scope. “Later” as a row action. Numbered step pips. Tiny provenance labels. Step counters in progress states.

title: Scale and tone.
text: 26px+ plain PR title (no chat bubble). Perplexity palette: warm off-white, teal accent, deep ink. Generous element size.

title: Alignment first.
text: Number, author, age, diffstat sit in fixed columns so every row lines up. Test: add a digit, swap a longer author name. Nothing else may move. Misalignment is the first thing he sees.

title: No tiny grey text.
text: Small uppercase labels, eyebrows, provenance lines, counters (“1 of 4 reviewed”, “Section 3 of 7”) are awful. Body-size ink or nothing. Never below 15px, never uppercase-tracked. A section label is one word: Summary.

title: One row anatomy everywhere.
text: A PR row is identical in Inbox, Tours, search: title, number, author, coloured diffstat, checks, age. Context-free counts (“7 sections”) never replace them.

title: Status words only where they vary.
text: A group titled “Ready to read” does not repeat Ready on each row. Failing / passing get a real icon, not a dot.

title: Swipe commits, tap opens.
text: Swipe left archives, swipe right opens the review, as full Mail-style gestures. No reveal-then-tap. Blur the displaced row content slightly. Keep clearance from anything revealed.

title: AI work looks alive.
text: In-progress analysis is a live, animated thinking indicator that feels smart. Never show the internal step. Make it tappable.

title: Analyze is one action, three outputs.
text: Analysing a PR = summary + per-file explanations + tour. Call it Analyze, not Write tour. An unanalysed PR is a real state with a visible way in. Per-file explanations show on the file rows.

title: Summary and Description, both first-class.
text: Description = what the author wrote. Summary = what the AI produced. One easy switch on the PR page.

title: Identifiers look like GitHub's.
text: Branches are squarish pills, head → base, tap to copy. Cites keep the concept but drop mono and the current pill style; try Mona Sans.

title: Counts: neither cards nor a run-on sentence.
text: No stat tiles, and no “+180 −32 across 4 files · 2 commits · 2 checks failing · 0 of 4 reviewed” either. Aligned label/value columns where nothing moves when digits change.

title: Sub-pages keep their context.
text: A tour section page carries the PR title and number in its header, with progress as a small element there. No pips, no eyebrow, no bottom “X of Y”.

title: Buttons are one line.
text: “Next unreviewed” becomes “Next”. A wrapped label is a defect.

title: Nothing overflows the frame.
text: No horizontal scroll, no scrollbar, nothing inside the 16px margin. Sliding rows clip inside the frame. Render at 390×844 before publishing.

title: Meta lines are one line.
text: Author · repo #number · age on one line; head → base on one line. Each segment ellipsises, nothing wraps.

title: Icons, not words, for segment navigation.
text: Overview / Changes / Tour is three icons in a capsule. Words are for tabs inside a page.

title: Summary / Description are underline tabs.
text: Pills are spent on chips, branches and cites.

title: The ⋯ sheet is on every PR screen.
text: Checks, GitHub, Analyze again; Approve, Request changes, Squash and merge, Merge when checks pass, Convert to draft, Close. Reachable from the PR, diff and tour headers.

title: Ask is a quiet toolbar.
text: “✦ Ask | ⋯” in a floating capsule beside the primary button. Never a second Ask inside a comment card. A sparkle alone is not a label: AI actions get a word or a real icon.

title: Tour sections scroll.
text: One scrolling page, no Next button. Progress is the ring in the header. Room at the bottom for the Ask toolbar.

title: Both swipes.
text: Right = Review (accent). Left = Archive (dark). Both commit, both blur the displaced row.

title: No avatars on list rows.
text: Identity on a row is the author name in its own column. The reader’s avatar lives in the inbox header; the author’s photo on the PR page.

title: Notes about a file look like comments.
text: An AI note on a diff is a comment card by “Pulls”: white, rounded, soft shadow. Not a loose line above the code.

title: Search is a bottom bar on every inbox.
text: Profile at the top, “Search or ask Pulls” floating at the bottom, no search icon in the header.

title: Two accepted row anatomies.
text: Canonical: P’s number column, then the title; author, checks, diffstat, age in fixed columns. Alternative: U’s status circle + number leading the row. Nothing else.

title: One real AI icon.
text: Withdrawn on 2026-10-14: Tavi said the sparkle does not stay, so no icon marks AI. AI actions are marked by their words ("Ask AI", "Analyze") and by the live progress indicator of rule 72. The text it had: an icon from a published set (Lucide sparkles), never a hand-drawn glyph, one per screen.

title: Tabs are an underline, not a box.
text: A hairline under Summary / Description and the accent underline on the active tab. No hairline above.

title: Cites sit on the text line.
text: Same cap height as the body, no vertical padding; tint and a thin border do the “different” work. Never taller than the line, never alone on a line.

title: Air between blocks.
text: A comment card or stats row never touches the diff. At least 24px above the diff’s top edge.

title: Checkboxes are bare.
text: Reviewed is a checkbox and a word. No pill, chip or border around it.

title: Tour position lives in a sticky strip.
text: N of M · title · ring is a sticky strip under the header; it updates as the next section reaches the top. The count exists only there, never inline above a section title.

title: Progress states show the work, not blanks.
text: No shimmer bars standing in for content. The live orb plus the outputs with their state: done, writing, pending.

title: Show states interactively.
text: Once a row is accepted, the next deliverable is a clickable prototype with real transitions: tabs, sheets, swipes, comment reply, the tour scroll.

title: Shadows match the canvas on every floating element.
text:
The header round buttons, the bottom search pill, the comment bar, the Tour card and the Ask bar all carry the canvas shadow (`floatShadow`). A missing or different shadow is a defect, not a nit. It was the most repeated complaint in the walkthrough.

On the phone today the shadows are there but faint and flat: a pale halo spread evenly round the edge, with no visible drop below it. The canvas shadow is faint too (8% ink on the round buttons), but it is pushed 2dp down (`0 2px 10px`), and that offset is what makes a button look lifted. The fix is a drawn shadow with a downward offset like the canvas, not a stronger glow. See Elevation & Depth.

Check: put each floating element beside Row W. Same shadow, with a visible drop below it, or fix it.

title: Blur is part of how things move, in three places.
text:
- Scroll edges: row titles blur as they scroll under the top header and under the bottom bar. Today every scroll edge is a hard cut: rows end in a sharp line under the chip row, text runs up to the bottom pill and stops, and content is sliced under a sheet's fixed header and under the diff's sub-header. The blur belongs at all of them.
- The swiped row blurs as it is displaced, as in the design. This is the same thing as rules 17 and 32. The canvas row moves sideways about 132 to 136dp with a 1.3px blur and a side shadow. Today it slides fully sharp, and the Review action is a flat teal rectangle with square corners and no shadow.
- The scope chips: switching between Waiting on you, Authored and All is liked and keeps its motion. It needs a blur transition, where the outgoing and incoming text overlap. The exact blur is not specified yet. Rule 67 is one possible reference.

title: Build to the canvas measurably. "Different" is a defect.
text:
"Close" is not accepted. What was flagged:

- Spacing inside Inbox rows, horizontal and vertical. The columns are not fixed (rule 13): the gap between the added and removed numbers changes from row to row, and the status marks sit at slightly different positions.
- A divider that the canvas has and the Inbox lacks: a line directly under the project heading. Tours has a hairline under its heading, and the Inbox draws hairlines only above later groups, so the group heading must be treated the same on every tab.
- The bottom search pill sits too low, with its lower edge almost on the system gesture bar. Raise it. The Ask bar on the Tour is in the same low position.
- On the Overview the top part is bigger in the design and is not stuck to the top of the phone.

Check: render the screen and the canvas row at the same size, side by side, before showing it. Measure gaps. Do not eyeball them.

title: Icons: keep the coloured Claude Code and Codex marks, cut the rest.
text:
- Only the Claude Code and Codex marks stay, in colour. Both are monochrome today, a black asterisk and a grey knot.
- The model is shown by its own icon. The Model row in the ⋯ sheet shows a robot head, and should show the icon of the model that was selected.
- No generic AI glyph, no decorative icon. The ones named so far: the robot head (on each Tours row, on the Overview's "Not analyzed yet" card and on the Model row), the sparkle (on "AI Analysis" in Settings and on "Ask AI" in the toolbar over a selected line), the compass (beside "Take a tour of this pull request" and inside the "Give me a tour" button), the chat bubble (in the Ask bar) and the speech bubble on "Request changes". By the same kind: the plug on Server, the layout glyphs on Unified and Split, the zoom magnifiers on Code size, and the globe, key and eye in the Server fields.
- Never the same icon twice on one card. Ask of every icon what fact it carries. This is rule 1 applied to icons.

The robot head also works as a status indicator, because the ring around it turns while a tour is writing. Not complained about: the three icons in the header capsule on the Overview, the gear, and the icons in the profile sheet.

Settled on 2026-10-14: the sparkle does not stay either, so rule 37 is withdrawn and no screen has an AI icon.

The `bans` check counts uses of the robot head, the sparkle, the compass and the chat bubble (`ai-glyph`), so new code cannot add one. The count may only fall.

title: One visual dialect: every screen is in the mobile style.
text:
A screen that looks like the old app is a defect. Seen on:

- Settings: font, spacing and pills differ from the rest, and it has the old icons. The sheet is a greyer cream than the Inbox, its close button is a bare ✕, and its segmented controls are the reverse of the Inbox capsule (rule 70). Its model selector must be the mobile one already made. Today it is a cramped dropdown that reads "Default (reco…" with "Default" shown twice.
- The Commands menu: flat rows straight on the cream with no cards, small grey icons, and rows cut by an ellipsis.
- The screen behind the project name: a breadcrumb, bare icons, a bordered filter box and select, and a loading spinner, with none of the round shadowed buttons.
- The file switcher in the Diff: plain grey counts that should be coloured as in the diff, a font that differs from the file name above it, and different files cut to the identical text.
- The toolbar that floats over a selected diff line, with a cut label and the sparkle (rule 48).

Reuse the components already built for mobile (model selector, sheets) instead of rebuilding a web version. The profile sheet is the reference for right.

Check: for every screen reachable from the main flow, ask "does this look like the old app?" before shipping.

title: Never make the reader wait for what the app already knows.
text: Opening a PR shows the title, the number and the rest of the header at once, because they are already loaded. Today a PR opens with "Checks None" and only two tabs, and the Conversation count and the real check state arrive a moment later, so the page fills in piece by piece. Moving between the Overview tabs has no load: content loads as the reader scrolls, the first items appear immediately, and the data is already fetched in the background. Which tab was meant is not named.

title: No loading screens. If something must wait, use skeletons.
text:
This is for page and list content whose shape is known. It does not override rule 43: AI work in progress (Analyzing) still shows the live orb and its outputs, with no shimmer bars.

Today opening a PR puts up an empty page with a spinner and "Loading pull request…", and the project screen does the same, although the title, number and author are already known from the row that was tapped. The Analyzing state puts shimmer bars under each file row, against the wording of rule 43. See the Decision log.

title: Refresh is silent.
text: Pull down must not show a refresh indicator. The app refreshes by itself and does not show it. Today the pull-to-refresh spinner is drawn on top of the first row's title, with no space reserved for it.

title: If it looks tappable, it does something.
text: The project heading on Tours looks tappable and does nothing: tapping it lights a grey press highlight across the heading and then nothing opens. It should open the project. On the Overview, the project name at the end of the meta line opens a screen in the old style, so the project destination must be in the new style (rule 49). The author name on the Overview does respond to a tap, which is right, and the branch chip copies the branch name. This is rule 4's "tappable rows look tappable", run the other way.

title: Tabs are easy to hit.
text: The tabs on the Overview are hard to hit. The hit area was not measured. Rule 12 asks for generous element size, and the kit's touch target is 44dp (`TOUCH`). In the frames the tabs are plain text labels with a teal underline under the active one, with no fill or padding, and "Conversation 23" runs close to the right edge.

title: The bottom pill is the one way to find a PR.
text:
- It reads "Search or ask Pulls" as in the design (rule 35). The app shows "Search pull requests" on the Inbox and "Search tours" on Tours. With the keyboard up the pill rides on top of it.
- It takes pasted links and PR numbers as well as text.
- So the "Open pull request" field in the profile sheet goes.

title: Row gestures are the same on Inbox and Tours.
text: Tours rows do nothing when swiped. They get a cancel on one side and open on the other, and tap still opens. This follows rules 15, 17 and 32: one row anatomy, both swipes, blur the displaced row. Today a Tours row is a robot icon in a ring, a one-line title cut with an ellipsis, and "Writing · about a minute" under it.

title: Swiping moves between the Overview tabs.
text: The Overview has three tabs: Summary, Description and Conversation (with a count). The canvas rules name only Summary and Description. Swiping left and right changes between them, with easy, clean swipes. Rule 9 still holds: files in the diff are never switched by horizontal swipe.

title: Sheets with long content pull all the way up.
text: Two bottom sheets cannot be pulled fully up. The ⋯ sheet is cut off at "Close pull request", with Review with AI, Review through a lens, Commands and Refresh below the fold, and the Select model sheet is cut off after Sonnet 5.5. The Ask sheet is nearly full height, so sheets are not all one height. Rule 5 prefers sheets over pages, so a sheet has to behave like a full surface when its content needs it. Sheets at their normal height are fine, the profile sheet included.

title: Menus and sheets open and close with a transition.
text: A menu in the Diff needs an open and a close transition. The menu at that moment is the Aa menu (Smaller, Default, Larger, Wrap long lines, Show review comments, Copy path, Open on GitHub, Load the whole file), not the file switcher. What is wrong with the motion is still Tavi's to say, and a reference showing how those transitions should look is pending. Rule 44 applies once it arrives. Rule 68 applies now: answer at once.

title: A control appears only where it works.
text: The Smaller / Default / Larger menu on the Tour does nothing there, so drop it. The Aa button on the Tour header opens it together with Wrap long lines and Show review comments, which are settings for code, and the Tour has no code on it. The same button on the Diff also holds Copy path, Open on GitHub and Load the whole file, which are fine. Same principle as rule 1: if it does not tell or do anything, cut it.

title: Commands is a designed menu in the app's style, with fewer things in it.
text:
- The current one is in the wrong style. Make a new design in the same style as everything else, and make it nice.
- It may hold too many things. "Review with AI" and "Review through lens" need a decision.
- Tentative, not a rule yet: open it on pull down.
- Open: how Commands relates to rule 29's ⋯ sheet. Today "Commands ›" is a row in the ⋯ sheet and in the profile sheet, and tapping it closes the sheet and opens the palette with the keyboard up. Whether it stays a row in the ⋯ sheet is Tavi's call.

title: Ask never needs Analyze first.
text: Tapping Ask opens the bottom sheet with the chat, and the reader chats straight away. The current screen is not acceptable: it is a title, one grey line reading "Analyze this pull request first, then you can ask about it.", a centred Analyze button, and no composer. Rule 19 makes an unanalysed PR a real state, so Ask has to work in that state.

title: AI actions answer the tap at once and never strand the reader.
text:
Pressing Analyze gave slow feedback. A double tap cancelled the run, and after the cancel there was no way to restart. The card then said "Analyzed" with the Tour step still an empty circle and an italic "Starting Claude…". Nothing said the run was stopped, and the only "Analyze again" was a tile inside the ⋯ sheet.

Checks:

- The first tap shows a response immediately.
- A second tap cannot cancel. Cancelling is a deliberate action.
- A cancelled or failed run always offers a way to start again.
- No state is a dead end.

title: The comment composer is a bar you type into.
text: Tapping a line of the diff opens a comment and in-review control at the bottom that is not liked. Two things appear together: a pill reading "Comment · In review ✕" between a round ‹ button and a round teal › button, and a small white toolbar floating over the selected line (rule 49). The words sit in a pill, so it reads as a label and not as a field you can type in. It used to be a bar you could just type in, which is better, and the buttons can be integrated into it. It is also missing its shadow (rule 45). A few variants are to be tried, so treat the form as open. This is the app-side counterpart of rule 10.

title: Reviewed moves you on.
text: Pressing Reviewed moves to the next file that is not reviewed, and marks the finished file, for example by greying it out a little. Today ticking Reviewed leaves the reader on the same file and shows a toast ("1 of 134 files reviewed") over the bottom of the diff. Back on the Overview the file is struck through and the button says "Review 133 files", so the count of what is left already updates. Rule 41 still holds: Reviewed itself stays a bare checkbox and a word.

title: One destination, one presentation.
text:
The same screen always opens the same way: always as a sheet, or always as a page. In the reference app the sign-in screen is a bottom sheet from one place and a full page from another, which is confusing. This extends rule 5: once a destination is a sheet, every route to it uses the sheet. In this app, check destinations that can be reached from more than one place, such as the model selector (rule 49).

Check: for each screen reachable from two or more places, open it from each. Same presentation every time.

title: A segmented pill moves its highlight, and the new content fades in.
text:
When a pill that switches between modes is tapped, the active highlight slides across to the new segment instead of jumping, and the new content fades in. This is the motion that goes with rule 27. It is one possible reference for the blur transition on the scope chips left open in rule 46, and it is not said to be the one.

Check: tap a segment. The highlight travels to it and the content fades in.

title: Reactive first, springy second.
text:
A control or sheet answers the instant it is touched. A spring or bounce is a bonus, not the requirement. A small bounce that fires the moment a character is typed was liked. This applies to rule 59 (transitions) and rule 63 (AI actions answer at once): sheets, the Analyze tap and the comment bar.

Check: tap or type and note how soon anything visibly changes. A plain transition that starts at once beats a springy one that starts late.

title: Elements that exist in both states keep their position.
text:
When a screen changes state, whatever is present in both states stays exactly where it was, so the change reads as a layer arriving instead of a new screen. In this app the nearest cases are the Overview header across the Tour (rule 23) and the bottom bar across screens.

Check: flip between two states of a screen and watch. Anything that exists in both must not jump.

title: The same control looks the same on a page and in a sheet.
text:
Confirmed by Tavi on 2026-10-14. In the reference app the round ✕ in a sheet is the same white circle with a soft shadow as the round buttons on the page behind it. In this app the Settings sheet had a bare ✕ and segmented controls that were the reverse of the Inbox capsule (rule 49), so one kind of control looked different on a page and in a sheet. Now a sheet's close and back buttons are the round white button with its shadow, and the segmented controls in a sheet are the Inbox capsule. Which way a segmented control goes is still Tavi's call: the canvas capsule is a white track with a grey selected segment, the reference app uses a grey track with a white selected segment, and the app follows the canvas until he says otherwise.

Check: take one kind of control (close button, segmented control, chip, round button). Find it on a page and in a sheet. Same shape, fill and shadow.

title: A live indicator may have shimmer bars under it.
text:
Rule 43 says no shimmer bars standing in for content. Tavi confirmed that bars are fine next to a live indicator, as in Perplexity's "Thinking…", where three grey bars sit under the mark and the word, the second and third a little shorter than the first. So the live indicator stays, and grey bars may sit under it as a hint of where the output will arrive. Bars never replace the indicator and never stand alone. Rule 51's skeletons for pages and lists whose shape is known are unchanged. The canvas text of rule 43 is unchanged.

Check: while AI work runs there is a live indicator on screen. Any bars sit under it.

title: Thinking text is a shimmering plain sentence with a dot.
text:
Tavi asked for the AI's thinking text to look more like Perplexity's. While work runs there is one line, a present-tense verb and the elapsed seconds ("Working 12s"; "Thinking" before the first step), the verb in the muted colour and the seconds in the faint one, in tabular digits, shimmering together. The shimmer leaves the text at full strength and dims a tilted band to a third of its opacity as it sweeps left to right, 1200ms a pass; with system animations off nothing sweeps. Each step is one plain sentence about the task, never the tool, in regular weight and never italic, after a 6dp dot in the text colour (red when it failed, amber for a warning) whose centre is 10dp in from the margin; the dot replaces every per-row icon. The live orb sits under the newest line on the dot's column at 16dp. When the line is replaced by another, the old one leaves upward through a 2px blur while the new one rises in from below, 150ms ease-in-out, 8dp of travel, a 50ms gap (transitions.dev, Thinking states). When work ends the shimmer stops and the line becomes "Worked for 2m 3s", a button with a chevron, right when folded and down when open, whose steps hang from a 1dp line that fades out. The sizes taken from screenshots are estimates, not measured on a device.

Check: start an analysis and watch it. One header line with the time, a dim band passing through it. Step lines with a dot, no icon, never italic. When the work ends, the shimmer stops and the line goes to the past tense with a chevron. With animations off nothing sweeps.

title: Motion uses one set of numbers.
text:
Tavi sent transitions.dev as the reference. Durations: 150ms for closes and text swaps, 250ms for opens, tabs and page slides, 350ms for a panel closing, 400ms for a panel opening. One easing, smooth out, `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`, for opens, closes and slides; ease-in-out for swaps; linear for shimmer. Blur is 2px for small things and 3px for page-sized changes. Scale is 0.97 for menus and 0.96 for dialogs. Travel is 4 to 8dp for text and pages. The mapping from the library's transitions to this app's surfaces was proposed by the rules file and Tavi can retune any row: menus use the dropdown recipe, dialogs the modal one, sheets panel reveal, the capsule tabs sliding, page changes page side-by-side, the thinking line shimmer text and thinking states. Looping effects follow the system setting "Remove animations".

Check: open and close one menu, one sheet, one dialog and one toast. Each takes the time above and eases out.
